statement: Every involution in the full once-punctured-torus loop-outer group has the global orientation multiplier plus or minus one, with the same sign as its 2-adic determinant. Therefore every finite subgroup generated by involutions has global orientation character.
where_proved: Part D, statement D.43; work/part_c/d43.tex; code/part_c/torus_involution_d43.py
depends_on: A.2; D.27; D.33; D.41; finite-index surface completion and class-two boundary-pairing comparisons
manuscript_passages: Part D(b) of the task; §24, folio 147 verso, scan 293; §30, folios 194–196, scans 383–387; §31, folios 198–199 verso, scans 391–394.
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The characteristic Heisenberg quotient, cusp filling, homology representations and finite inner conjugation are all given by explicit maps.
notes: An odd-prime Heisenberg cover has closed homology module 2 trivial plus regular minus the central-coset permutation module. Every nontrivial central-character block has odd dimension q squared. A negative sign at q exchanges paired blocks, and the determinant of the alternating-pairing identity forces the negative sign at every prime. At q=3 a positive sign normalizes the finite action to identity or simultaneous inversion; its rational Schrödinger implementer and the Galois-paired odd-dimensional multiplicity spaces force the 2-adic sign positive. No hyperelliptic centrality or unproved finite-order lift adjustment is used.
